sources.title: Soda bread
sources.observation: The source explains that in soda bread, the lactic acid in buttermilk reacts with baking soda to produce carbon dioxide bubbles, which leaven the dough. It adds that such quick breads can rise quickly and reliably without the time and labor required for kneaded yeast breads.

sources.title: Bread, beer and wine: Yeast domestication in the Saccharomyces sensu stricto complex
sources.observation: The authors state that yeasts in the Saccharomyces sensu stricto complex convert sugars into ethanol and CO2 via fermentation, and have been used for thousands of years to ferment foods and beverages, including bread. They add that it is unknown when humans began consciously adding selected yeast to make bread.
